en: The Ocean of Ḍākinīs, the Ocean of Ḍākinīs.
Listen, listen! A mind that has fallen into conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*) and is not desirous [of liberation] cannot be a deliverer.
You are of the nature of illusion (*māyā*); thus you are the deliverer of the entire triple world.
II.

For here indeed there is neither existence nor non-existence, neither passion nor dispassion; one does not become impassioned again toward that which is equanimous. Since this dharma is established in the middle, do not be impassioned; rejoice in the indestructible dharma, O Vajra!
(III) Where both merit and demerit have set, there you fix your mind upon awakening.
For he becomes a perfected one (siddha) among gods and asuras, and his own movements transcend both decay and arrival.
First, the Lord Vairocana is situated in the navel, endowed with the downward-moving quality (*adhoguṇa*).
May his breath rise as far as the throat, so that he may become like a lamp illuminating the three worlds.
Any other mantra is "with another," such as up to the moon being grasped on the left;
for a mantra adorned with the bindu is one thing, while the other is called a mantra that generates the Yoginī.
Furthermore, it is said that there are two [functions]: meditation, which is killing and giving life.
Indeed, when two drops are situated at the sides, or a drop is situated on the head.

The seed-syllable situated at the end of the *ya*-group is the vehicle for this path of great awakening; it is the seed-syllable of Śūkarī. It possesses the ornament of the letter *ā* as an ear-ornament, and the ornament of the sun situated in the half of the sixteen digits.
The seed-syllable is the first of the *ya*-group, conjoined with the qualities of the world of Heramba,
adorned with the thirteenth vowel, and indeed the digit of the bright fortnight.
Indeed, the fourth is the bliss that shines forth together with *tila*.
Indeed,
that class whose end is of the nature of *sukha*, joined with the vowel *u* and the crescent moon (*candrabindu*), has a flame fixed upon its head.
Furthermore, let the day indeed consist of the syllables together with the *parā* [state],

seated upon the sun-throne (*ravyāsana*), grasping the fourth vowel; let the ear-region be adorned by the digit, the half-moon, and the bindu, which is the intrinsic nature at the end of passion (*rāga*).
The syllable of gnosis, doubled, is born from the day of the Sambhara;
situated above and below, it is the seed-syllable, the grasping by the Lord, for it is indeed the Sambhoga.
Joined with the ritual of wealth, the seed-syllable *santrāṃsanī* [is used];
*phaṭ phaṭ* should be uttered at the end once again.
Indeed, kindle the splendor (*dyuti*)—let that splendor enter through the opening of the city.
O Caṇḍāvatī, shine forth and fill the three worlds; therein the *bodhicitta* arises.
The abiding nature is Vairocana; the intrinsic nature is the Dharmadhātu, which is indeed the form of the effect.

Established as the *ta*-group, it is the fifth syllable; the fifth group is the support of space (*nabhas*), having the form of the Yoginīs. The seed-syllable at the end of the *pa*-group, conjoined with the vowel *au*, is indeed the destroyer of delusion.
And the host of Yoginīs flashes forth;
furthermore, the fourth seed-syllable of that group, the refuge of the Yoginīs, pervades the three worlds.
The third seed-syllable of the first [group] is the wheel of Tāyinī, which causes the destruction of the six destinies;
it is the seed of awakening, the final letter of the *ya*-class. The first seed-syllable of the fifth [group] is that of *tathatā*.
The seed-syllable *i* resides upon the head; it is the accumulated syllable of water, the causal state of all things.
The seed-syllable situated in the middle of the *ca*-group is taken together with the sun and moon, characterized by the specific activity of blazing.
May the seed-syllable of Vārāhī, the letter *A*, which is immeasurable and of the nature of the wisdom of the three worlds, touch the ear.
The seed-syllable of Agni, joined with the second vowel (*Ā*), is the nature of the karma of saṃsāra.
The seed-syllable *Sa* together with the vowel *I* touches the head; it is always seen as the nature of Brahman.
The second vowel is to be grasped, like the form of Tāyinī who delivers sentient beings. Furthermore,
the letter *ra* situated in the *ya*-group is joined with the vowel *a*.
The three elements joined with the vowel *i* cause the Yoginī to quiver.
The first seed-syllable (*bīja*) of the sixth group is the complete essential nature of the Yoginī-mantra.
May the seed-syllable situated in *ra*, joined with the vowel *a*, become the cause of the destruction of wicked beings.
The letter *ja*, having taken the vowel *i* and being conjoined with the state of *māyā*,
is the seed of the tooth; the vowel *e* adheres to the ear as the seed of the snake-mantra, which is distinct from that [tooth].
The syllable O is indeed the entire element, the mantra of the excellence of gnosis.
And LA, when conjoined, is the support of the world and the causal dharma for awakening.
The seed-syllable preceded by KA and joined with the seat of YA is certainly not distinct from the nature of deathlessness.
One should perceive the end of the *pa* group, not established by a vowel, whose essential nature is the three worlds;
that syllable, adorned with the letter *e*, is easily grasped.
Furthermore, the end of *pa* is the middle, the innate nature (*sahajasvarūpa*) which is immeasurable.
Therein, the letter *ī* joined with *sa* and *para* is the primordial wisdom (*jñāna*) of Vajrasattva.
Joined with the vowel *i*, the end of the *ya*-group is "destroyed" (*vinaṣṭaka*), the nature of which is ignorance (*ajñāna*).

That mantra, which is the intrinsic nature of phenomena (*dharmasvabhāva*), pervades the entire intrinsic nature. The syllable *sa* carries [the breath] from the aperture; it is the seed-syllable of conveyance (*vahana-bīja*) conjoined with the Sun (*ravi*).
The mantra whose intrinsic nature is *makaranda* consists of the fourth letter of the *pa*-group (*pha*) as the seed-syllable, seated upon the vowel *ū*. Indeed, it is the destroyer of fear.
That mantra destroys the enemy; furthermore, [it is formed] from the *pa*-group...
The fourth [seed-syllable] is the great *rava-rava*. (p34-35) The seed-syllable of the wind, together with the letter *ā*, is light, like a jewel within a mantra.
The seed-syllable *apyam* (ap), grasped in the ear, is the form of illusion (*māyā*). Joined with the supreme letter *e*, it is the cause of the wandering in the three worlds.
Indeed, the final letter of the *pa*-group (*ma*) is the seed-syllable whose nature is marrow (*majjā*).
Together with the letter *a* and the supreme letter *a*, it is the nature of wonder;
for the end of the *ya*-group is indeed the seed-syllable of the lotus-letter.
The central seed-syllable of the *ca*-group, situated upon the head of the letter *ra*, with the vowel *e* attached after it— this is the nature of both the god and the asura.
Thus, indeed, is the six-footed mantra, the assembly of Yoginīs, and the wheel which is the very form of all ritual actions.
VI.
Indeed, the final letter of the *ya*-group is the seed-syllable whose intrinsic nature is awakening (*bodhi*), and it is joined with a line of two tongues.
The *yoginī* mantra consists of the vowels;
the seed-syllable (*bīja*) established therein is *acalakā*.
Indeed, the letter *na* joined with the letter *e* is the signless state of all beings.
May the first Lord of Qualities, the empowered vowel *a*, and the double-tongued vowel *i*— the very nature of the constituent elements of the three worlds— descend upon my head.

Indeed, the letter *ta* joined with the letter *e* is the first seed-syllable (*bīja*) of the fifth group; it is indeed the essential nature (*tattvasvarūpa*) of the Yoginīs. The seed-syllable situated as the fourth of the *ya*-group is the feminine nature (*nārīsvabhāva*) of all.
The first seed-syllable of the eighth group is adorned with the void and consists of the semen element;
the first seed-syllable situated in the second group is established upon the drop of the skeleton.
The second seed-syllable of the *ya*-group, joined with the vowel *i*, is the Lord situated in the fire of the vajra;
its end (the seed-syllable) is adorned with the letter *e* and beautifully embellished by the womb (*yonis*).
The letter *ta* joined with *ra* is the king that destroys fever;
the letter *bha* joined with *ra* and adorned with the vowel *e*, situated within the vessel of the navel.
The seed-syllable ending in *pa* has the nature of the vital point (*marman*); the seed-syllable ending in *ṭa* is the state of plowing and is adorned with *i*.
It is the mantra for drying up, possessing the nature of the four joys, the seed of the great treasure.
The seed-syllable of Ravi, adorned with the vowel *o*, has the nature of the Ruṣṭi channel;
the second seed-syllable of the *śa*-group is the form of the Heart.
The letter *ṇi* is grasped in its own essential form as the nature of the reality of the Yoginīs.

Indeed, the syllable resulting from the conjunction of *ka*, *ra*, and *a* is the state of the essence of the far-reaching channel (*dūranāḍī*). Having grasped the seed-syllable situated between *ta* and *pa*—
The group of Yoginīs is the eight-syllable form of the sādhana itself;
the final letter of the *tavarga* adorned with the vowel *i* is the form of the central channel of the skull-cup.
The syllable *ka* which is grasped causes that karma to perish;
and the syllable *ra*, grasped by the letter *a*, is to be released from the center of the head with a great roar.
Indeed, the seed-syllable of the Earth (*la*), joined with the letter *i*, resides in the center of the triangle.
Indeed, the seed-syllable at the end of the *ta*-group stands above the emanation (*nirmāṇa*) and is adorned with the vowel *i*.
It is indeed a conjunction of the syllables *ta*, *ra*, and *a*.

The seed-syllable is the dharmadhātu, the triangle, and the origin of the three worlds. Indeed, that [syllable] is grasped as the middle one together with semen; for the nature of gnosis is conjoined with the syllables *na* and *i*.
The final letter of the *pa*-group (*ma*), adorned with the vowel *a*, is the lotus at the navel of Māyā.
The Sun, who resides in the letter *ya* and possesses the nature of *karṇa*,
and the seed-syllable at the end of the *ṭa*-group (*ṭha*) joined with *i*— the Lord grasps this as the entirety of undifferentiated existence.
Thus, this ten-word mantra is the destroyer of all four ages;
for the first dharma is indeed the solar seat preceded by the letter *pa*.

The fourth letter situated therein (the seed-syllable), adorned with the letter *e* upon its ear, is the mantra of the Yoginī. The seed-syllable situated in the middle of the *ta*-group (the letter *da*) signifies the Beloved (*Dayitā*).
Indeed, the conjunction of the letter *na* with the letter *i* is the churner of the universe.
The letter *pa* together with *pra-pañca*, the letter *ra* accompanied by *i*, that which possesses the circle of Yoginīs (*yoginī-cakravān*),
the seed-syllable taken from the middle of *ca*, and the syllable *ja* according to its form.
Established in the wind (the letter *ya*) and conjoined with the letter *e*, it has the nature of ego (*ahaṅkāra*).
It is the end of the *ya*-group, adorned on its head with the third vowel, and is the very essence of the knowledge of the entire mantra.
The seed-syllable *ja* is the mantra of radiant form.
The letter *ya* joined with the vowel *e* (*ye*) is the illustration for all vehicles.
The third seed-syllable of the *ca*-group (*ja*) is the awakening to the form of such a Yoginī;
the end of the *pa*-group (*ma*) is the seat situated as the fourth of that group,
[which belongs to] all the gurus of the mantra.
The mantra *ta* joined with the third vowel (*i*) has the nature of awakening without remainder.
The third letter of the sibilants (*ṣa*) is indeed the seat of *ta*; it carries across the world of the dull-witted.
The seed-syllable *sta* is taken from the earth, having the form of fourteen *kara*s;
it is the mantra known as the *yoginīsaṅketaka*.
The final letter of the *pa*-group (*pha*), the seed-syllable *i*, may it touch the shaven head in the form of liberation from the ignorance of the universe;
and the supreme subsequent seed-syllable is the intrinsic nature of Vajrasattva.
The syllable *ni* is the negation of both dharma and adharma;
the final [syllable] of the *ya*-group (*na*) is the seed-syllable whose form is the sky-clad Yoginī.
The letter *ja*, possessing the seat of *ra*, arises with the nature of *śukra*.
Furthermore, the letter *a* is at the end of the wind; born of *ojas*, it is the form of Brahmā and the lotus.
The Sun is indeed non-conjoined and of an imperishable nature;
it bears the form of the entire Yoginī, situated at the head of the third vowel with the supreme seed-syllable.
For the letter *ma* is the form of the central principle (*madhyatattva*).
He utters the face of the Yoginī-form, which is spoken with the syllable *a* following [the letter *pa*].
The letter *pa*, adorned with the crown of the syllable *o*, is indeed the intrinsic nature of the form of Sahaja.
The seed-syllable situated in the middle of the *ka*-group (*ka-varga*), adorned on its head with the third vowel, has the nature of the banner of reality (*tattva*).
The syllable *gi* is the knowledge of that which is devoid of intrinsic nature (*niḥsvabhāva*).
The first [seed-syllable] of the second group, illuminated by the letter *a*, is the realm of desire (*kāmadhātu*).
The end of the *pa*-group joined with *e* is the illusory nature (*māyāsvabhāva*) of the whole.
Furthermore, the end of the seed-syllable of the semi-vowels (*antaḥstha*) and the end of the *pa*-group constitute the seat (*āsana*), which is inseparable from semen and wind.
The seed-syllable of Pāvaka (Ra) is entwined with the vowel *i*, and its form is like a perfected illusion (*māyā*).
The second seed-syllable of the *Ka*-group (Kha) is the reflection of the Sky-Yoginī;
its lateral seed-syllable is the vowel *e*, adorned with an ear-ornament, moving and solitary.
Thus, the wheel has the nature of space.
The "nine-word" is the collection of Yoginīs; it is the syllabic form of the mantra, which is the triple world.
VIII.
For that mantra is a double conjunction; it is the seed-syllable of fire and wind situated in *pa*, the passion of great bliss.
Of that (*pa*-group), the second seed-syllable is filled with the vowel *a*, which indeed has the nature of the four great elements. It is the union of the syllables *pa*, *ra*, and *o*.
The syllable *akṣara* consists of three [letters] whose nature is wind (*pavana*).
Furthermore, that [syllable] joined with *aṃ* is the seed of consciousness (*vijñāna*).
That seed situated in the middle of *ka* is indeed adorned by the ear-ornament of *e*.

The true nature of the *yoginī-mudrā* is as follows: furthermore, that which is called "the word" (*pada*) is inseparable from the means (*upāya*). It is not merely a mantra; furthermore, that which is called "the word" is the form of both emanation (*utpatti*) and reabsorption (*saṃhāra*).
The single seed of *pa-ra-a* is the ultimate reality (*paramārtha*). For the end of *ṭa* is the seed joined with *ā*, and from that, non-killing arises. For the end of *ta* crushes everything.
The third vowel situated after *kā* and *ka* occurs in the third [position], marked with a bindu; this is the invocation of all the Yoginīs.
Likewise, the syllable *kha* and the syllable *na* are situated in the third [position].
The third vowel is not present there; it has the form of a hand raised in exhaustion.
Furthermore, the mantra-word should be recited twice, which destroys all discursive thoughts.
Indeed, the syllable *ya* is the mantra that adorns the vajra-aperture.
The seed-syllable situated between the letter *ca* and established upon the seat of the Sun (*ra*) brings about the destruction of delusion;
it is the one with the supreme (*sa*) in the middle of the unstruck (*anāhata*).
The third of the *śa*-group (*ha*) is established upon the seat of *ha*.
The syllable *e* as an ear-ornament, the *ḍākinī*-mantra, and the "obstructing all" [syllables];

the mantra-word for "dry up," which is to be recited twice; the destruction of the ego of the knower, and the reality of awakening and non-awakening—such is the twelve-word nature of the earth, the very essence of the yogic practice.
The second seed-syllable of the *ka*-group is the reality of the assembly of Yoginīs; the syllable *ṭa* is taken, with *pa* at its end as the seat, adorned with the vowel *aṃ* as a crown.
By the letter *a*, there is the fulfillment of that mantra, which is the very nature of the six destinies (*ṣaḍgati*).
The seed-syllable situated in the middle of *ka*—by means of that seed-syllable, poison indeed becomes internalized.
And the seed-syllable *ka* has the nature of emptiness (*śūnya*).

The seed-syllable of the Earth, ending with the letter *ra* and completed with the vowel *a*, is [flanked] by *agni-jvāla* (the fire-flame, *ha*) and *īśāna* (the lord, *ha*). By that, the Great Lord moves.
Furthermore, the seed-syllable situated as the fourth of the *ta*-group is adorned with the vowel *a*.
The form devoid of *bhava* (the letter *ha*). *Ravi* (the letter *ra*) joined with *i* (*ri*). Indeed, the *vetāla* is the union of *ra* and *i*.
The end of *ṭa* (the letter *ṭa*), when taken as the seed-syllable and adorned on its head with the third vowel (*u*), [becomes *ṭu*].

By its power, the entire triple world dies; for it perceives the end of the seed. By that, the mind is thoroughly known and rendered supreme. When joined with the word "A," the net of mantra-born [conceptions] is shattered.
The two *ma*s and the two *hā*s should be recited as "hara hara," which is the nature of delusion (*moha*).
The seed-syllable *pa* adorned with *i*, and the syllable *pi*, are lost when grasping at all suchness (*sarvatathatā*).
Indeed, the syllable *sa* joined with *i* is the mantra devoured by the lion.
Indeed, that mantra is the birth of the Immortal. At the end of *pa*, there is the borrowed *a* with a bindu; let it rest upon the crown. The cause is the conceptualization of death.
The letter *sa* together with the second vowel (*i*) moves in conjunction; this is the prior preparation.
The seed-syllable situated on *śa* is the cremation ground;
for its end is the syllable joined with *i*, which is the absence of intrinsic nature (*niḥsvabhāva*) in all things.
The end of the *pa*-group (the seed-syllable) is filled with a vowel; it is the great grasping of the corrupted mind.
The syllable *u* does not cause the arousal of discursive thought (*vitarka*).
The second seed-syllable of the *pa*-group, the syllable *ā*, should be joined to the head; that which is situated at the mark is the *sādhya-bodhi-mantra*, and that is the *apāna*.
The two-syllabled mantra consisting of the syllables *ta* and *ra* is indeed terrifying to the world;
the single seed-syllable *pa-ra-a* destroys the distress and exhaustion of the thirty-three [gods].
The knowledge that ends with *ya*, which is sequential and divine (*dastra*), is indeed pure.
The seed-syllable *ṇa* (ṇa-kṣara), established as the letter *e*,
is the ear-ornament that destroys improper knowledge;
the syllable *sa* (sa-kṣara), which completes the letter *a*, is the cessation of the flow of the breath.
Indeed, the mantra "Na" is adorned at its head by the third vowel; thus, the nature of both dharma and adharma is overturned.
The yogi who meditates on the mantra of meditation has his own essential nature as the object of contemplation. Having grasped its end—the seed—it appears as non-existence, like a city in a dream.
The second seed-syllable of Pavana is that by which the state of delusion is to be incinerated;
it is the letter *sa* differentiated by the vowel *i*, the destroyer of the lion and the buffalo,
and the seed-syllable situated in the Sun, the king of all Yoginīs.
For the seed-syllable ending in *pa* is adorned with the vowel *a*;
by that, the magician has subdued all sentient beings.
The letter *u* is the adornment of the seed-syllable on the earth; such a seed-syllable is one in which the knowledge of reality has been attained.
Thus, these fourteen syllables indeed constitute the mantra of Māraka for the ignorance of all sentient beings;
the seed-syllable *ka* is in the middle, with *ra* as its seat, and *ya* at the very beginning is the sustaining dharma.

The third [syllable] of this is *bindu* on the head (*masta*), and its second letter is joined with the vowel *i*; by that, the yoga of the non-Buddhists (*tīrthika*) is destroyed. The letter *ta* signifies awakening (*bodhana*).
The fourth letter of the *ta*-group (*dha*) joined with the vowel *ā* is the incantation-seed (*bīja*) for infinite awakening;
the letter situated in *ra* (*ra*) adorned with the third vowel (*i*) is indeed the entire *ri*-mantra, the captor of the Yoginīs.
For the path of the Yoginī is adorned with the *na*-mantra and the syllable *i*. The six-word phrase of the *sumbha* mantra should be recited twice; it is the reality of awakening.
Likewise, the *sumbha* mantra is the very nature of the worship of the Yoginīs.
The *hana*-mantra (*pada*) should be recited twice for the destruction of minor obstacles and their persistence.
The single syllable *pa-ra-a* is indeed the individual nature of each sense faculty;
*ṇa-a-aṃ* is the full seed-syllable of the quality (*guṇa*), which is the mantra.
The letter *sa* (by it), the entire [system] is indeed bound by the channels;
together with the letter *ra*,
the word *pavamatra* was set forth from the sky.
The seed-syllable established in the letter *sa* is the form of all things;
the seed-syllable ending in *ya* is indeed filled with the knowledge of the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*).
For the mantra of the letter *na* is filled [with that], whereby awakening is not conceptualized anywhere.
There, a *tilaka* is seen upon the forehead;
for the seed-syllable ending in *pa* is indeed of a great sweet form.
It is filled with the supreme *ā*, and by it [is performed] prostration at the feet of the assembly of Yoginīs.
For the seed-syllable ending in *pa* is joined with the vowel *ā* and adorned with the jewel of the letter *aṃ* on its crown; it is the very nature of the gift of all Dharmas.
The letter *sa* is the excellent Dharma, the subduer of ignorance.
The *ce-cha* mantra is the Bodhisattva; by it, non-arising (*anutpatti*) is reached within cyclic existence (*saṃsāra*).
And the seed-syllable situated in the middle—the letter *da*—does not shine forth as something meaningless.
The letter *na*, conjoined with *i*, is the state of world-weariness (*arati*) for all beings without exception.
The *kroḥ*-mantra is the assault that cuts through cyclic existence;
the seed-syllable *dha* is the shattering of all conceptual proliferation for every sentient being;
and the seed-syllable *mū* is the delusion of all worldly activity.
Thus, the mantra consisting of four lines beginning with "the arising of the channels of the wheel" and so forth, [is recited] when the jar of ritual action is victorious, victorious. XI.
The *ti*-mantra is indeed the innate nature (*sahaja-svarūpa*); the *upakarma-viśeṣa* is indeed all the wheels (*sarvacakra*).
The *daṃṣṭrākarālinī*-mantra is the nature of the activity (*karma*) of the worlds.
The *ma*-mantra, the *hā*-mantra, and the *mudrikā*-mantra are the nature of the ears (*karṇa*).
The mantra-word for the foremost queen of the deity Śrī Heruka is the nature of the nose;
the mantra for the thousand-headed one is the nature of the lord of vowels;
the mantra-syllable for the thousand-armed one is the nature of the body.
For by means of the mantra, a single wheel [is formed] hundreds of times;
the mantra of the ḍākinīs has the nature of the arising of death.
XII
The mantra *sahasrānane* is the object of form;
the mantra-word *jvalitatejase* is the object of the mind;
the word *jvālāmukhi* is the object of the body.
The mantra *piṅgalalocane* is eye-consciousness;
the mantra-word *vajraśarīre* is body-consciousness;
the mantra *vajrakāsana* is attached to the object of the nose.
The joined word is olfactory consciousness;
the mantra *cili* has the lord of vowels (*svarapati*) as its object;
the mantra *he* (the word) is to be uttered twice, and it has sound as its object.
The lord of the vowels for sound, and consciousness for the two;
thus the seven-word mantra, mixed with half [the syllable], is the form of the birth and death of all.
XIII.

Following that, one should twice recite the seed-syllable (*bīja*) which has the sixth vowel as its seat, adorned with a crescent moon and a drop (*bindu*) as its crown; it is Vajrasattva, the Guhyaka (in the form of the Guhyaka).
It consists of two *kha*s, two *dhu*s, two *muru*s, the state of action (*karman*), and the state of being (*bhāva*), all situated together with the vital breaths (*prāṇa*).
The mantra syllables recited by the great yoginīs of non-duality, which constitute the form of the other body, are:
the two syllables *dreṃ* and *dhaṃ*; the two syllables *graṃ*; the two syllables *he*; and the two syllables *ha*.
The ten syllables of the Wrathful One (Krodha) are to be understood as Yamāntaka and the others.
Let the fourth seed-syllable of the *pa*-group, the vowel *ī*, touch the head;
this is the mantra of *me-sa*, the junction of all, the nature of the Ḍākinīs.
Thus, the twelve mantra-syllables are indeed attached to the state of the preta-being;
the six mantra-syllables *hasa-hasavīre* are the seed of suchness (*tathatā*) and the infinite exposition of qualities.

The syllable *hā* consists of four seed-syllables; *ho* is one; *huṃ* is two—these seven syllables should be recited. For the element of one's own nature (*svatva-dhātu*) begins with the skin and so forth. "Destroyer of the three worlds" is the mantra that indeed subdues wicked speech.
The mantra surrounded by one hundred thousand ten million Tathāgatas,
adorned with the *ūsvara* (the letter *u*) together with its own vowel (*para*),
and embellished with the crescent moon and the bindu— thus should the mantra be properly invoked.
For the entire nature of the mantra consists of the syllables HA, Ū, AṂ, and HI.
Thus, from these four mantra words, there arises the accomplishment born of the generation of the Yoginī.
XV
Furthermore, by means of the ritual procedure, he expands the seed-syllable of reality, which has a seat situated at the side of the five vowels, is adorned with the crescent moon and the bindu,
and possesses a seed-syllable situated at the side of the letter *pa*, [thereby] spreading the net of Yoginīs.
The syllable *ṭa* is the incantation for kindling.
In the form of a lion, the mantra-syllable *khaḥ* destroys Vināyaka.
In the form of an elephant, the mantra *gaḥ* causes obstacles to living beings.

The mantra consisting of the two words "trailokyodare" and "pada," the origin of all the Vārāhī messengers; the mantra consisting of the two words "sasudramekhale" and "agra," which is the girdle-mantra of Sāgaramekhalā;
and the syllables "hūṃ phaṭ," which are the lords of the Ḍākinīs.
From the non-duality of the Hero (Vīra), the syllable of the mantra *huṃ* should be understood as its manifestation and its application according to yoga.
Thus, the seven-syllable mantra brings about the arising of the stage of knowledge that illuminates all ritual actions and worlds, and it causes the mind to abandon [dualistic grasping].
XVI
The word *huṃ-hā*, the great deluder of beasts, is cyclic existence (*saṃsāra*);
through yoga, you are the mantra whose form is peace.
You are the word of praise for the worlds of the *ḍākinīs*; the world is like the radiance of awakening.
In the rite of truth (*satyakarman*), the mantra-syllables *huṃ* and *phaṭ* are shown in the fourth case;
the phrase "terrifier of spirits" destroys the knowledge of the non-Buddhists (*tīrthika*).
Thus, the seven mantra-syllables perform the activity of differentiation.
The end of the letter *pa* is indeed joined with *sa*, and the end of the letter *ya* is joined with the Lord *ī*.
Thus, the end of the syllable *na* joined with the letter *ra*, and the word *siddhe* at the end of the syllable *pa*— this is the *vidyāpada* of the *Śvarī-mantra*. Furthermore,
the seed-syllable *ṭa* is placed beside the syllable *pa*, followed by *huḥ*, adorned with a crescent moon and a bindu.
It should be stated again:
the syllable *ṭa* is situated at the side (*pa*), along with *huṃ*, *phaṭ*, and *svāhā*.
Thus, the mantra is said to be situated at the navel according to the rule, together with the name *svadhā*.
XVIII.

Let the object of the senses not be seen; for there is neither enjoyment nor form and so forth. Having grasped the entire manifold world as mere appearance, vomit it out; abandon delusion and enter into the ultimate reality.
XIX.
Delight, delight in the Vajra of supreme great bliss! Accomplishment is to be achieved through wisdom and means.
Cultivate compassion for the worlds among all gods and asuras, for you are bound [to them] as it were.
The Holder of the Vajra of Awakening has indeed been propitiated by means of great bliss; for what [else] are you in the meditative absorption of emptiness?
Delight the vajra in the lotus today, for by that you awaken together with him in the meditative absorption of emptiness.
O Lord, ignite the seed-syllables of the four elements; Caṇḍālī arises, ready within the Avadhūtī.
The three worlds are burning, yet no one is seen; it blazes, it blazes in the nature of nirvāṇa.
The ḍākinī rejoices in the form of the innate (*sahaja*); the appearance of aging and death is not seen.
O mind, realize this awakening and deliver the realm of sentient beings from illusion!
All people are indeed deluded regarding the nature of enlightenment; they are fools, truly ignorant.
But that person who [abides] in the reality of the Yoginī, the essence of all things—he is indeed Vajradhara.
Listen, listen, sister! For you are the liberator from the intrinsic nature of the realm of sentient beings;
there is no distinction among your beings, for you are the savior of every hero.
XXII.
By the syllable *Śū*, the world is gladdened; remember the reality that is the innate nature (*sahaja-svabhāva*).
Again, for one who does so, the suffering of cyclic existence (*saṃsāra*) does not arise; such a person is indeed a Buddha, though appearing as a common being (*paśu*).
XXIII.

You are a yogī, a messenger of Yama; there you shall indeed attain that which is free from old age and death. One who has attained unsurpassed awakening does not undergo death; such a yoginī is joined with neither sin nor merit.
O you who have generated the sense faculties as Bodhisattvas, make the objects of the senses into Buddhahood!
You who uphold the aggregate whose nature is that of the Buddha, you who uphold the elements as the Vajra-holder.
For bondage consists of coming and going; you uphold the immortal state in its entirety.
By virtue of your compassion, you are such.
In whatever way you may do service for others.
XXV.
O Lord, you who are invited by the world day and night, who are you that have entered into emptiness?
Arise, O you whose nature is compassion; for my sake, O Vajradhara, do you desire great bliss?
Listen, listen, O you who are devoted to the welfare of others! Just as the world of living beings dies, you must desire the blooming lotus; in that way, may you bring happiness to the entire world.
Delight, O Vajradhara, delight in me; for the innate nature (*sahajasvarūpa*) is ineffable.
Just as you are empty and devoid of activity, so too does the world of beings (*sattvaloka*) enter into supreme union.

For you are indeed the cause of all phenomena; who are you? You are the innate nature that is unapproachable. Love me according to the ultimate truth, so that you may proceed as you do throughout the world.
XXVI.
The mandala-circle is the state of great bliss; therein are twelve yogis, and therein there is neither merit nor sin.
Consider every conceptual thought in its own true nature, and recognize bliss within that mandala.
You consider the sensory delusion to be great bliss; that is the nature of another at that moment, not of yourself.
O you who manifest the mandala-circle throughout the three worlds, act by destroying whatever takes various forms!
Dwell in the nature of the circle of Yoginīs, which is the state of great bliss and the supreme joy of the world.
The world of deluded beings does not go to the state beyond sorrow;
having taken hold of the Sahaja-Sundarī, one abides in great bliss.
For every person in the three worlds possesses the nature of a Buddha.
O enemy, delight in the nature of the maiden Compassion!
Since you do not cultivate the ultimate reality, you will indeed never attain Buddhahood. O enemy! 0!
Know indeed that there is no distinction between the internal and the external;
you are able to carry across and deliver the entire world. Ari. 0.
XXVIII.
Only the innate nature (*sahajasvabhāva*) is indicated here; indeed, [it belongs to] the Lord of the three worlds, including gods and asuras.
The world of the senses does not know where the supreme great bliss (*paramamahāsukha*) is; worship it with this verse.
All karma is like the form of an entity; where then is existence not seen as nirvāṇa?
You are not deluded by illusion in the navel; where does it destroy the vehicle of sentient beings today?
